To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

prognostic factors are of great value in the management of breast cancer and that the Nottingham Prognostic Index is the most accurate prognostic index currently available for use in routine histopathological practice.

prognostic factors in breast cancer include the following: (1) histological type, (2) histological grade, (3) oestrogen receptor status, (4) progesterone receptor status, (5) S-phase fraction, (6) DNA ploidy, (7) HER2 status.

1) The Nottingham Prognostic Index is a useful tool for predicting outcome in patients with breast cancer; 2) The Nottingham Progestrone Receptor Score (NP) is a reliable and accurate method for measuring the level of progesterone receptor in breast cancer; 3) The NP is a useful predictor of response to endocrine therapy and survival in breast cancer patients with oestrogen receptor positive tumours.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the understanding and application of prognostic factors in breast cancer.
the development of new and better ways of assessing breast cancers and the application of these methods in the management of breast cancer.
the development of new methods of diagnosis of breast cancer and the assessment of prognostic factors in primary and metastatic disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the following prognostic and therapeutic factors are important in the routine assessment and management of patients with primary breast cancer: histopathological tumour type (ductal or lobular carcinoma), tumour grade, tumour size, axillary node status, oestrogen receptor status, progesterone receptor status, S-phase fraction and ploidy status.
prognostic and therapeutic factors are of great importance in the management of breast cancer.
prognostic factors are of value in determining which patients are at greatest risk and therefore need the most aggressive treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
prognostic and predicative factors are important in breast cancer management, but the value of many of them is still to be determined.
the Nottingham Prognostic Index is a useful and simple tool in predicting the risk of recurrence in patients with primary operable breast cancer.
prognostic factors are important in the selection of patients for adjuvant systemic treatment, and in the selection of appropriate endocrine therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need for further prospective validation of prognostic factors in order to improve their clinical applicability.
there is no single factor that is of overriding importance in the management of breast cancer.
the use of prognostic factors in the management is a complex and evolving field and the role of histopathology is crucial in the process.
